# Story 01 — Seat Selection & Temporary Reservation Hold (Story: 3)

## Prerequisites

- Requires the auth feature to be in place: `src/app/core/auth/auth.service.ts`, `src/app/core/auth/auth.guard.ts`, `src/app/core/auth/auth.interceptor.ts`, and `src/app/core/models/auth.model.ts` already exist in the repo — read them fully before writing any reservation code so the new feature reuses the same authentication primitives (current-user state, guard redirect pattern, HTTP error interceptor) instead of duplicating them.
- Requires the movies/screenings feature to be in place: `src/app/features/movies/models/movie.model.ts`, `src/app/features/movies/services/movie.service.ts`, and `src/app/features/movies/movie-details/movie-details.component.ts` already exist — this story's seat-selection route hangs off a screening reached from movie details, so read these to confirm the exact shape of a "screening" object (id, hall reference, price, start time) before defining the reservation models.

Treat `src/app/features/movies/` and `src/app/core/auth/` as the structural precedent: mirror their `models.ts` / `service.ts` / component folder split when building `src/app/features/reservation/`.
- **Backend dependency:** this story assumes the backend exposes `GET /api/screenings/{screeningId}/seats` and `POST /api/reservations` with response shapes close to the examples in the intake. ## Story Goal

Deliver an Angular feature that lets an authenticated customer, starting from a screening (reached via the existing movies feature), view seat availability for that screening's hall, select exactly one available seat, submit a temporary reservation hold to the backend, watch a 10-minute countdown based on the backend's `expiresAt`, and proceed to a checkout page carrying the `reservationId`. The frontend never invents seat availability — it always defers to backend responses for both the initial seat map and the outcome of the hold request (including conflicts).

Not in scope:
- The actual checkout/payment page implementation beyond a route target that receives `reservationId` (a placeholder route/component is acceptable; full payment flow is a separate story).
- Multi-seat selection UI beyond a single seat per reservation (the intake's examples show multiple seats in the JSON payload, but requirement 5 explicitly restricts the frontend to "one available seat per user reservation" — implement single-seat selection and send `seatNumbers` as a one-element array).
- Backend implementation of seat availability, hold expiry, or reservation persistence — this plan is frontend-only.

## Implementation tasks

### 1 — Reservation models

Create file: `src/app/features/reservation/models/reservation.model.ts`

Define, using the field-naming convention confirmed in `src/app/features/movies/models/movie.model.ts` and `src/app/core/models/auth.model.ts`:

```typescript
export interface SeatAvailabilityResponse {
  screeningId: string;
  numberOfSeats: number;      // confirm exact field name against backend/hall model read in step 6
  unavailableSeatNumbers: number[]; // confirm exact field name against actual backend contract
  pricePerSeat: number;       // confirm against screening model read in step 6
}

export type SeatState = 'available' | 'selected' | 'held' | 'reserved';

export interface CreateReservationRequest {
  screeningId: string;
  seatNumbers: number[]; // single-element array per requirement 5
}

export type ReservationStatus = 'Held' | 'Expired' | 'Cancelled' | 'Confirmed';

export interface ReservationResponse {
  reservationId: string;
  status: ReservationStatus;
  expiresAt: string; // ISO date string, e.g. "2026-08-28T21:10:00"
  screeningId: string;
  seatNumbers: number[];
  totalAmount: number;
}
```

**Note:** the exact field names of `SeatAvailabilityResponse` are not given precisely in the intake beyond "the response should allow the frontend to determine which seat numbers are currently unavailable" — the executor must confirm the real backend contract before finalizing this interface, and update all call sites if names differ.

### 2 — Reservation HTTP service

Create file: `src/app/features/reservation/services/reservation.service.ts`

Mirror the HttpClient/base-URL/error-handling pattern found in `src/app/features/movies/services/movie.service.ts` (confirmed in Context step 7). Expose:

```typescript
getSeatAvailability(screeningId: string): Observable<SeatAvailabilityResponse>
createReservation(request: CreateReservationRequest): Observable<ReservationResponse>
```

- `getSeatAvailability` calls `GET /api/screenings/{screeningId}/seats`.
- `createReservation` calls `POST /api/reservations`.
- Map HTTP errors using the same idiom confirmed via the `catchError`/`HttpErrorResponse` grep in Context step 11. At minimum distinguish:
  - `400` → generic "invalid request" message, do not retry automatically.
  - `401` → let the existing `auth.interceptor.ts` behavior handle it (confirm in step 4); if it does not already redirect, redirect to login here.
  - `404` → "This screening/reservation no longer exists." — used by both the seat-selection page (screening not found) and the checkout/summary page (reservation not found).
  - `409` → conflict — the caller (seat-selection component) treats this as "seat no longer available," not a generic error.
  - `500` → generic error message with a retry affordance; do not change local state on 500.

### 3 — Reservation state service

Create file: `src/app/features/reservation/services/reservation-state.service.ts`

This service owns the minimum state list from the intake: `screening`, `seats`, `selectedSeat`, `price`, `totalAmount`, `reservationId`, `reservationStatus`, `expiresAt`. Implement with Angular signals (consistent with the "RxJS and/or Angular Signals" technology note and to keep individual seat components free of global state, per the intake's explicit instruction).

Responsibilities:
- `loadSeatAvailability(screeningId)`: calls `ReservationService.getSeatAvailability`, populates `seats` (a computed array of `{ seatNumber: number; state: SeatState }` built from `numberOfSeats` and `unavailableSeatNumbers`), and resets `selectedSeat` to `null`.
- `selectSeat(seatNumber)` / `deselectSeat()`: only mutate `selectedSeat` when the target seat's state is `available`; no-op otherwise (enforces requirement 5's "prevent selecting unavailable seat").
- `createHold(screeningId)`: calls `ReservationService.createReservation` with `{ screeningId, seatNumbers: [selectedSeat] }`; on success stores `reservationId`, `reservationStatus`, `expiresAt`, `totalAmount`; on `409` re-invokes `loadSeatAvailability` and surfaces a conflict flag/message instead of throwing.
- **Persistence for refresh/navigation (requirement 11):** persist `reservationId` (and `screeningId`) to `sessionStorage` (or `localStorage`, whichever the executor confirms is already used elsewhere in the app — grep for `sessionStorage`/`localStorage` in `src/app/core/auth/` first, since the auth token storage mechanism is the natural precedent to reuse) immediately after a successful hold. On service construction / route entry, if a `reservationId` exists in storage for the current screening, do not assume it is still valid — the summary/checkout component must re-fetch reservation status from the backend before trusting it (the backend remains the source of truth; do not add a "get reservation by id" call if the backend contract from the intake does not define one — flag this to the backend owner as an open dependency).
- Countdown: expose a computed/derived value (e.g. `secondsRemaining`) driven by comparing `expiresAt` to `Date.now()` on an interval (e.g. `setInterval`/`interval(1000)`), stopping and setting `reservationStatus` to an expired state locally once `secondsRemaining <= 0`. This is purely a UI countdown — do **not** call any "release seat" endpoint from the frontend on expiry (per requirement 9's explicit "must not attempt to release seats merely by changing local UI state"); instead, after expiry, re-call `loadSeatAvailability` so the seat map reflects backend truth.

### 4 — Seat selection component

Create files: `src/app/features/reservation/seat-selection/seat-selection.component.ts`, `.html`, `.css`

- Standalone component (match the standalone/module style used in `movie-details.component.ts`, confirmed in Context step 8).
- Reads `movieId` and `screeningId` from the route (matching whatever `ActivatedRoute` pattern `movie-details.component.ts` uses).
- On init, calls `ReservationStateService.loadSeatAvailability(screeningId)`.
- Template: render a grid of seat cells from `1` to `numberOfSeats`. Build the grid so the last (remainder) row is centered — compute a fixed number of columns (e.g. a near-square/rectangular layout) and, for the final partial row, add empty/centering placeholder cells or CSS `justify-content: center` on that row's flex container so the remainder seats sit in the middle rather than left-aligned.
- Each seat cell is a small square, colored per state:
  - `available` → green, clickable.
  - `selected` (the current user's chosen seat) → pink, clickable to deselect.
  - `held` or `reserved` (any other unavailable state) → gray with an "×" centered in the cell, not clickable.
- Below the grid, show `Selected Seat: {{ selectedSeat }}` and `Price: {{ price }} EGP` only when a seat is selected (from `pricePerSeat` in the loaded `SeatAvailabilityResponse`, or the screening's price field if seat map doesn't carry price — confirm during step 6 read).
- A "Continue" / "Hold Seat" button, disabled when no seat is selected, calls `ReservationStateService.createHold(screeningId)`.
- On `409` conflict result from `createHold`, display the exact message from the intake: `"Sorry, one or selected seat are no longer available. Please select different seat."`, and rely on the state service's automatic re-fetch to update the grid.
- On successful hold, navigate to the reservation summary/checkout route, passing `reservationId` (e.g. `router.navigate(['/reservations', reservationId])` or embedding it as a route param — pick a path consistent with `app.routes.ts`'s existing param style confirmed in step 1).

### 5 — Reservation summary / countdown component

Create files: `src/app/features/reservation/reservation-summary/reservation-summary.component.ts`, `.html`, `.css`

- Route receives `reservationId` as a param.
- Displays the held seat number, `totalAmount`, and a live countdown formatted as `Seats held for: MM:SS`, driven by `ReservationStateService`'s `secondsRemaining`.
- When the countdown reaches zero, display `"Your seat hold has expired. Please select your seat again."`, disable any "Continue to Checkout" action, and provide a link/button back to the seat-selection route for the same screening (requirement 9).
- "Continue to Checkout" button is enabled only while `reservationStatus === 'Held'` and `secondsRemaining > 0`; navigates to the checkout route (placeholder route acceptable per Story Goal's out-of-scope note) carrying `reservationId`.
- On component init, if the state service does not already hold the matching `reservationId` in memory (e.g. after a page refresh), do not treat the reservation as valid purely from storage — the component must be resilient to a missing/mismatched in-memory state and should show an appropriate loading/error UI rather than assuming "Held" status (requirement 11). Since the intake does not define a `GET /api/reservations/{id}` endpoint, flag this as an open backend dependency in code comments and, until it exists, fall back to using the persisted `expiresAt`/`reservationId` from storage read in task 3, clearly noting in a comment that this is not re-validated against the backend.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Unauthenticated user opens seat-selection URL directly** — the `reservationGuard` (task 6) must redirect to login before the component loads, and login must return the user to the same seat-selection URL (requirement 12). Verify this via the return-URL mechanism confirmed in `login.component.ts` (Context step 9).
- **Seat becomes unavailable between load and selection click** — `ReservationStateService.selectSeat` (task 3) checks the seat's current in-memory state before allowing selection, but this only protects against stale local clicks; the authoritative check still happens server-side on `POST /api/reservations`. The `createHold` 409 branch (task 3) is the real enforcement point.
- **Reservation conflict (409) on hold creation** — do not navigate to the summary page; display the exact intake message and re-run `loadSeatAvailability` so the seat that lost the race is shown as unavailable (task 3, task 4).
- **Countdown reaches zero while user is on the summary page** — stop the timer, set local `reservationStatus` to expired, disable "Continue to Checkout", show the expiry message, and trigger a fresh `loadSeatAvailability` call if the user navigates back to seat selection (task 5, task 3). Do not call any release/cancel endpoint — none is defined in the intake.
- **Browser refresh on the summary page** — in-memory Angular state is lost; the component must re-derive at least `reservationId` from the route param and fall back to persisted storage (task 3/5) rather than assuming the reservation is still valid without any backend confirmation, since no `GET /api/reservations/{id}` endpoint is confirmed in the intake. Document this gap explicitly in code comments.
- **Opening the checkout/summary page directly without ever selecting seats** — `reservationId` route param exists but no local or stored state matches it; show an error/loading state rather than fabricating seat/price data (task 5).
- **Backend `500` on either endpoint** — show a generic error message and allow the user to retry the same action (reload seats or resubmit hold) without losing their current seat selection (task 2, task 4).
- **Backend `404`** — screening no longer exists (seat-selection entry) or reservation no longer exists (summary entry); show a distinct "no longer exists" message per requirement 13 and do not allow retry of the same id (task 2).
- **`numberOfSeats` not evenly divisible by the chosen column count** — the seat grid's last row has fewer seats than the row width; center that row via layout, not by hiding seats (task 4, requirement 2).
- **User rapidly double-clicks "Continue" on seat selection** — disable the button immediately on click (before the HTTP call resolves) to avoid firing duplicate `POST /api/reservations` calls for the same seat (task 4).

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Authenticated customer can navigate from movie details to `/movies/{movieId}/screenings/{screeningId}/seats` and see a seat grid sized to the hall's `numberOfSeats`.
- [ ] `GET /api/screenings/{screeningId}/seats` is called on page entry via `reservation.service.ts`.
- [ ] Seats render in green (available), pink (selected by current user), and gray-with-× (held/reserved/unavailable) per requirement 3.
- [ ] Only one seat can be selected at a time; selecting an unavailable seat is a no-op; selecting then clicking the same seat deselects it.
- [ ] Selected seat number and price are displayed together once a seat is chosen.
- [ ] `POST /api/reservations` is called with the selected seat when the customer proceeds.
- [ ] A `409` response shows the exact conflict message from the intake, refreshes availability, and lets the customer pick another seat without navigating away.
- [ ] A successful hold navigates to the reservation summary route with `reservationId` and shows a `MM:SS` countdown derived from `expiresAt`.
- [ ] Countdown reaching zero disables "Continue to Checkout" and shows the expiry message, with no frontend call attempting to release the seat.
- [ ] Unauthenticated access to the seat-selection route redirects to login and returns to the same screening after login.
- [ ] `400/401/404/409/500` responses each produce the documented distinct behavior from task 2.
- [ ] Refreshing the summary page does not silently present an expired/invalid reservation as an active hold without accounting for backend truth (documented limitation noted in code where a status-check endpoint is not yet available).
